title: Portrait and Bell
premise: Mirabel Halloran, a rationalist schoolteacher, arrives in the village of Cold Ash with his family and discovers children vanishing one per generation, each disappearance marked by the ringing of a bell that was melted down in 1911. The village's founding families have been feeding the missing to something beneath the church to preserve their power, and the count of the vanished is nearly complete. When Mirabel's own daughter is taken, he must abandon his disbelief, ally with the last honest descendant of the founders, and descend beneath the church to break the count before the final toll. He saves her, but at the cost of taking the old sexton's place as the bell's keeper — justice rendered outside any law, and a corruption he can feel beginning in himself.
about_author: Wren Lockridge is the pen name of a former village schoolteacher who spent a decade collecting oral histories of vanished children across rural England. Portrait and Bell is their second novel, written in a converted chapel where, they insist, nothing has ever rung.

chapters.title: The Long Road to Cold Ash
chapters.summary: Mirabel Halloran's POV. He drives his wife Senna and daughter Ivy into fog-bound Cold Ash to take the schoolmaster post, noting the village's too-perfect politeness and the church tower's empty belfry. Emotional beat: cautious hope shadowed by an unnameable wrongness.

chapters.title: Twenty-Nine Empty Desks
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. His first day teaching reveals enrollment records listing children no villager will name; the caretaker, Mrs. Tarnow, burns a ledger page before he can read it. Emotional beat: professional curiosity curdling into unease.

chapters.title: What the Bell Was Made Of
chapters.summary: Ivy's POV. Exploring the churchyard, Ivy finds a scrap of green-tarnished bronze shaped like a mouth and hears humming from inside the locked tower. Emotional beat: childlike wonder tipping toward dread.

chapters.title: A History of Generous Families
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. In the parish archive he learns of the 1911 melting of the Bell of Saint Aldhelm and a pattern: every twenty-two years, one child 'goes to service' and never returns. Emotional beat: the historian's thrill giving way to horror.

chapters.title: The Welcome Supper
chapters.summary: Senna's POV. At a dinner hosted by squire Edmund Vasey-Hale, the village elite toast Mirabel's arrival with unsettling precision, and Senna notices every guest wears a small bronze button. Emotional beat: social discomfort becoming quiet alarm.

chapters.title: First Toll
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs braided together. At midnight the melted bell rings once; dogs howl, lights kindle in windows, and the Vasey-Hales stand in their garden facing the church. A child's desk sits empty at dawn. Emotional beat: collective complicity exposed.

chapters.title: Nobody Is Missing
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. He reports the vanished boy to the constable, who produces paperwork proving the child never existed; even the mother smiles blankly. Emotional beat: the vertigo of gaslighting and institutional erasure.

chapters.title: The Sexton's Confession
chapters.summary: Old sexton Ambrose Pell's POV. Dying and guilt-ridden, Ambrose tells Mirabel the founders' bargain: feed the bell a child each cycle and it keeps the village prosperous and the founders powerful. Emotional beat: shame seeking absolution.

chapters.title: Buttons and Bronze
chapters.summary: Senna's POV. Senna traces the bronze buttons to a foundry that cast the bell's replacement clapper in secret, discovering the Vasey-Hales kept a piece of the original metal. Emotional beat: determination hardening.

chapters.title: Ivy Counts the Names
chapters.summary: Ivy's POV. Ivy copies the carved names hidden under the school piano — twenty-one children — and realizes the newest carving is half-finished, waiting for its letters. Emotional beat: innocence confronting predation.

chapters.title: The Twenty-Second Year
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel confronts Edmund Vasey-Hale, who offers him partnership, wealth, and silence, revealing the count completes this year and the bell 'chooses.' Emotional beat: temptation met with fury.

chapters.title: A Door Nailed Shut
chapters.summary: Ambrose's POV. Ambrose shows Mirabel the bricked crypt stair beneath the vestry and gives him the sexton's iron key, warning that the bell below is not a bell but a throat. Emotional beat: passing the burden.

chapters.title: They Took My Daughter
chapters.summary: Mirabel and Senna alternating POV. After the family tries to flee, the road loops back to Cold Ash endlessly; at dawn Ivy's bed holds only a half-finished carving of her name. Emotional beat: devastation and resolve fused.

chapters.title: The Village That Watches
chapters.summary: Senna's POV. Senna rallies the two other non-founder families, but neighbors report them, and one ally is found smiling blankly, wearing a bronze button. Emotional beat: isolation sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: What Ambrose Kept
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Among Ambrose's effects Mirabel finds sixty years of the sexton's records proving the founders murdered their own children first, and a diagram of the crypt's true geometry. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into evidence.

chapters.title: The Unmaking of Edmund
chapters.summary: Edmund Vasey-Hale's POV. Edmund prepares the final rite, but the bell's hunger turns on him, showing him what prosperity actually costs; he wavers between legacy and terror. Emotional beat: power revealed as servitude.

chapters.title: Down the Throat of the Church
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel breaks the brickwork and descends through bone-lined passages toward a cavern where twenty-one children stand unmoving around a suspended mass of molten-slow bronze. Emotional beat: courage past the edge of reason.

chapters.title: The Counting House Below
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The bell speaks in the voices of the vanished, offering Ivy back if a keeper takes Ambrose's place forever; Mirabel sees the corruption already blooming in his own reflection. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen with open eyes.

chapters.title: Toll Twenty-Two
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. As the founders begin the rite above, Mirabel shatters the original bronze fragment Senna recovered, and the false count collapses; the standing children wake and climb toward light while the tower splits. Emotional beat: catharsis through ruin.

chapters.title: Justice Without a Courtroom
chapters.summary: Senna's POV. With the crypt exposed, the surviving founders are given to the villagers' judgment outside any law; some flee, some kneel, none are forgiven. Emotional beat: grim, necessary reckoning.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Post
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Ivy wakes whole, but the bell must be kept silent by a bound keeper; Mirabel takes the iron key and the vow, feeling the first cold weight settle into his chest. Emotional beat: love priced honestly.

chapters.title: Portrait and Bell
chapters.summary: Ivy's POV, years later. Ivy, now grown, paints the church and visits the sexton's cottage where her father tends the silence, still himself, still watching; she leaves a finished carving of all twenty-two names. Emotional beat: mourning braided with peace.
